# Taking Email Back » Linux Magazine

- How New Open Source Mail Servers and Clients Make Self-Hosting Practical Again The fourth in a five-part series on European-funded open source projects in hardware and software. Taking Email Back Photo by Chris G. on Unsplash Author(s): Jeffrey A. McGuire The fourth in a five-part series on European-funded open source projects in hardware and software. Three Homes, No Data Center Deuxfleurs, a French nonprofit, keeps its servers in members' homes in Lille, Nantes, and Massy: two or three second-hand Lenovo ThinkCentre mini PCs each, with a copy of the same data so its websites stay up when one of them loses power or fiber line. Quentin Dufour, one of the founders, says some major French websites already serve their pages from this setup. Next, the collective wants its email to work the same way. The software for self-hosting email in this manner is called Aerogramme, and it isn't finished. Deuxfleurs still runs its own mail on Dovecot, a long-established open source mail server, and plans to move to Aerogramme around January 2027. The collective is heading the opposite way from almost everyone else. According to the independent daily DNS measurements published by RIPE Labs, email for the million busiest domains on the web has consolidated dramatically: In 2016, 44.6 percent of these domains used small or self-hosted servers, and that share halved to 22.4 percent by July 2026. Small regional hosting companies and independents are losing accounts to corporate providers like Google and Microsoft, who together handled 38.6 percent of these busy domains. Email is older than the Internet itself, and it still runs on open standards anyone can implement. Any server can deliver to any other, and any standards-compliant client can read any mailbox. It’s the hosting that has concentrated into a very few hands, eroding autonomy and giving hosting providers power over the data that travels through digital correspondence. Two cases illustrate how this can limit operational independence. In May 2025, staff at the International Criminal Court (ICC) told the Associated Press that the court's chief prosecutor lost access to his Microsoft email account after he was named in US sanctions; Microsoft denies suspending services but hasn’t explained what happened to his account. In February 2026, the Dutch government told its parliament that the tax administration was moving about 40,000 workplaces to Microsoft 365 for lack of a short-term alternative, while acknowledging that Microsoft could be forced under state pressure to stop delivering services. The Dutch government reversed course in October: The tax administration, customs, and the benefits agency will run mail and calendar on their own servers from 2027, with European open source tools for storage and collaboration to follow. The question now: How are developers working to decentralize email hosting on a wider scale? Each obstacle pushing organizations off of small or self-hosted email servers has open source projects working on a solution. Three of them show how the pieces fit; all of them supported by NGI Zero, the EU-funded programs that enable open source research and development. How Email Got Away from Us In the 1990s, running your own mail server was ordinary. Universities and small companies did it, and so did Mauro De Gennaro. In 1993, as a teenager, he fetched mail for users of his bulletin board over UUCP: the dial-up protocol Unix machines used to exchange mail. He has worked on mail software for most of the three decades since. When he looked at the open source stack again about six years ago, he saw "it's the same software that companies and servers have been using for over 20 years." He counts 12 separate programs to run a conventional self-hosted setup. Each has its own configuration format and logs, written by different people in different styles. The software works well, he says, but was "designed and documented for other developers." Bundles such as Mailcow and Mail-in-a-Box install the whole set at once: “They abstract the complexity," De Gennaro says, "but they do not remove it." Since all of it was designed for a single machine, running it as a cluster server is possible in the same way it's possible to take a Fiat Cinquecento and turn it electric: "It was not designed for that." Google launched Gmail into that friction in 2004, with a gigabyte of free storage, and let companies run their own domain's mail on it. "Then they started billing," De Gennaro says. The users were captive, and moving email is disruptive enough that few of them left. Ben Bucksch joined the Mozilla mail team in the late 1990s, where his first contribution made email links clickable; he also served in leadership for the Thunderbird Council and invented AutoConfig, which lets a mail client set up an account from nothing but an email address. In his telling, the lock-in started within the client. IT departments think about email as servers; “what users want is to keep their workflow," Bucksch says. Microsoft shaped those workflows with Outlook's calendar and corporate features: Outlook works properly only with Microsoft Exchange, and Microsoft is pushing Exchange customers into its cloud. By some estimates, about 75 percent of professional mailboxes are on Office 365. "If we want to free the lock-in," he says, "we need to start with the client." Dufour and Armaël Guéneau of Deuxfleurs locate the problem in operations. IMAP is the protocol most clients use to read mail. An IMAP server has to serve webmail that queries the server for every view, desktop clients such as Thunderbird that synchronize whole mailboxes, and phones that do some of each. Implementing it is hard; the reliability people expect is harder. When the tax office sends you an email, Dufour says, "it must work." The expertise to run mail at that level, Guéneau says, "tends to be captured by hyperscalers." As Dufour tells it, Google didn't adapt existing mail software; it built Gmail on top of its distributed storage. Open source mail software was designed for one machine first, so adding distribution later, he says, requires "really huge trade-offs." Reclaiming email is more complex than deciding to run your own server and navigating the software. Your service has to fluently speak with the large providers and support migration without disrupting service. And, of course, it needs sustainable funding. Today, publicly funded teams are working on solving each of those three problems. Rebuilding Server, Client, and Storage Stalwart, the server from De Gennaro’s team, focuses on streamlining the software to replace 12 programs with one: Installation takes two commands and a six-screen web wizard. It speaks every common mail and collaboration protocol: SMTP for sending, IMAP and POP3 for reading, JMAP for web-based mail, and CalDAV and CardDAV for calendars and contacts. Spam filtering, sender authentication, and TLS encryption are built in. Give it a token for a DNS provider such as Cloudflare or Route 53, and the server publishes its own mail records. Behind the wizard are nearly 3,000 settings across 176 screens, which most operators never touch. De Gennaro calls Stalwart "the software at the other end of your email client or calendar client." Stalwart 1.0 was released in October 2026 after five and a half years of development. NGI Zero funded the project with two grants: one for the mail server, and one for calendars, contacts, and file storage. For users who can’t leave Outlook features behind, there’s Parula. Keeping the application logic strictly separate from a thin interface layer, and a well thought-out common logic, so a new protocol takes “just a few thousand lines of code,” Bucksch and his team at Beonex GmbH built an Outlook-like interface alongside a modern interface, a chat-style view and a classic three-pane view. It runs on a JMAP server or any other mail server and offers shared team mailboxes, delegated access so an assistant can run a manager’s calendar, and free/busy lookups for team meetings. It speaks IMAP, JMAP, and POP3, plus four from Microsoft: Exchange Web Services (EWS), Exchange ActiveSync, Microsoft Graph, and Outlook Web Access. Partially funded by NGI Zero, Parula also removes a dependence most people never notice. Multi-factor login typically runs through Google's or Microsoft's identity services; an AutoConfig extension allows a client to discover and log in directly to an organization's own identity server. Bucksch says that Parula is the first desktop client that does this. Aerogramme, an IMAP server that doesn't keep any state of its own, answers the operations problem in the storage. It doesn’t send or receive mail, so it needs a separate mail transfer agent such as Postfix; then it encrypts each mailbox on Garage, compatible with Amazon’s S3 interface. Garage replicates every piece of data in three locations, so users can still read and write their mail if a site goes offline. This design for power cuts and residential Internet connections gave up perfect synchronization, but it spreads maintenance work among five to ten members rather than requiring one big server host to give up all his weekends. The research problem, Dufour says, is mapping the mail, calendar, and contact protocols cleanly onto object storage. Aerogramme is still on the way, with internal deployment planned for January 2027 and a public beta a few months later. To get there, a second grant funded through NGI Zero is supporting a hunt for edge cases where a network delay or a failure halfway through writing could lose a message. The three projects already interoperate with each other and with other email programs on the NLnet list funded by NGI Zero. Parula lists Stalwart as a supported server; Stalwart can keep its messages in Garage. Bucksch and De Gennaro both name Mox as another server built as a single package. Different teams, working separately, have split the email problem and built solutions that fit back together. 1 2 3 4 Next » Buy Linux Magazine SINGLE ISSUES Print Issues Digital Issues SUBSCRIPTIONS Print Subscriptions Digital Subscriptions Related content Internet Research Group Proposes Better Email Standard Improvements to SMTP will provide better guarantee of confidentiality more »

feedText: These tiny, hollow molecular structures act like miniature reaction chambers to trap molecules and accelerate chemical reactions. The cages showed enormous differences in performance, with the best catalysts more than 10,000 times more active than the least effective ones.
articleBody: Chemistry researchers have developed a new way to identify and understand highly effective artificial enzyme-like catalysts using powerful "molecular cages" that mimic the behavior of nature's enzymes. These tiny, hollow molecular structures act like miniature reaction chambers to trap molecules and accelerate chemical reactions. The cages showed enormous differences in performance, with the best catalysts more than 10,000 times more active than the least effective ones.

subtitle: Researchers from the Xinjiang Astronomical Observatory of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have discovered a binary system in a field used to calibrate the JWST's optics.
feedText: Researchers from the Xinjiang Astronomical Observatory of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have discovered a binary system in a field used to calibrate the JWST's optics.
articleBody:
# Astronomers Discover a Hidden Binary in a Star System Used to Calibrate the JWST

When observatories like the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) conduct observation campaigns, they often start by observing star fields to calibrate their instruments. These stars must have precisely characterized spectra so that their radiant energy (or fluxes) can be measured accurately. However, some stars that appear as single objects have a binary companion that has not been resolved, altering their predicted stellar flux. In fact, a star that is used for JWST calibration (HD 158485), which was thought to be an A-type star, has been identified as a binary system .

The discovery was made by a team from the Xinjiang Astronomical Observatory of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), who found the binary while reviewing long-term observations from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). Their study, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters , provides the first orbital solution and dynamical mass ratio for the system. HD 158485 is an example of a pulsating, variable, or Delta (δ) Scuti star, which experiences brightness changes at a regular frequency (typically every 18 minutes to 8 hours)

From the TESS data, the team noticed that HD 158485 was pulsing in six distinct rhythms, otherwise known as δ Scuti pulsation modes. They further noticed that these pulses fell into two groups with opposing light-travel-time variations, meaning that the light from these pulses reached Earth at different times. This could only be explained by the presence of a binary companion. The team used the variation between the two signals to trace the star's orbital motion with HD 158485, which showed that they orbit each other every 382.8 days.

Pulsation timing results for HD 158485. The two groups of pulsation modes show opposite time delays, revealing the orbital motion of both stars. Credit: Chenglong, LV et al. (2026).

The data also allowed them to constrain the orbital parameters and the star's mass. According to their calculations, the companion has an eccentricity of 0.242, indicating a moderately elongated, closed elliptical orbit, and is about 80% as massive as its primary - making it a likely F-type (yellow-white) main-sequence star. Their findings are independently confirmed by an orbital model built from earlier TESS data, which accurately predicted the timing variations that were detected by a separate observation campaign.

The team further compared a two-star atmosphere model with a conventional single-star model using the system's mass ratio, which showed a flux difference of about 1.6% between one and five micrometers (μm), and 2.5% between five and 28 μm. These findings could have significant implications where JWST calibration is concerned. While they do not represent a measured error, they do show how mistaking a binary system for a single star can shift predicted fluxes, thus throwing off readings.

In essence, the team's results show that stellar pulsations can reveal binaries that conventional observations leave unresolved. It also underscores the need to account for hidden stellar companions when evaluating calibration standards for our instruments.

Further Reading: Chinese Academy of Sciences

His work is featured in The Ross 248 Project and Interstellar Travel edited by NASA alumni Les Johnson and Ken Roy. He also hosts the podcast series Stories from Space on Patreon. He lives in beautiful British Columbia with his wife and family. For more information, check out his website .

title: SAP: IT-Sicherheitsvorfall bei SAP – „Haben verdächtige Aktivitäten identifiziert“
subtitle: „Verdächtige Aktivitäten“ bei SAP: Der Softwarehersteller meldet einen Zwischenfall.
feedText: Serverraum: Nach Handelsblatt-Informationen betrifft der IT-Sicherheitsvorfall bei SAP die Softwareentwicklung. (Symbolbild) Foto: AP Düsseldorf. SAP ist von einem IT-Sicherheitsvorfall betroffen: Der Softwarehersteller hat nach eigenen Angaben „verdächtige Aktivitäten“ identifiziert und Gegenmaßnahmen ergriffen. Nach aktuellem Stand der Untersuchung gebe es keine Hinweise auf einen unbefugten Zugriff auf die Geschäftsdaten von Kunden, teilte der Konzern am Donnerstagabend mit. Zuvor hatte der „Spiegel“ über einen „Hackerangriff“ berichtet. Details wie den Angriffsweg oder mögliche Täter nannte SAP nicht.
articleBody:
# SAP: IT-Sicherheitsvorfall bei SAP – „Haben verdächtige Aktivitäten identifiziert“

Serverraum: Nach Handelsblatt-Informationen betrifft der IT-Sicherheitsvorfall bei SAP die Softwareentwicklung. (Symbolbild) Foto: AP Düsseldorf. SAP ist von einem IT-Sicherheitsvorfall betroffen: Der Softwarehersteller hat nach eigenen Angaben „verdächtige Aktivitäten“ identifiziert und Gegenmaßnahmen ergriffen. Nach aktuellem Stand der Untersuchung gebe es keine Hinweise auf einen unbefugten Zugriff auf die Geschäftsdaten von Kunden, teilte der Konzern am Donnerstagabend mit. Zuvor hatte der „Spiegel“ über einen „Hackerangriff“ berichtet.

Details wie den Angriffsweg oder mögliche Täter nannte SAP nicht. Nach Handelsblatt-Informationen aus Konzernkreisen ist die Softwareentwicklung betroffen. Unter dem internen Namen „Project Granite“ veranlasste der Softwarehersteller demnach mehrere Sofortmaßnahmen zum Schutz der Entwicklungsinfrastruktur. Zahlreiche Teams seien davon betroffen.

SAP setzt in der Produktentwicklung die Plattform Github ein, auf der Programmierer Programmcode speichern und gemeinsam bearbeiten können. Der „Spiegel“ berichtete unter Berufung auf einen Insider, dass die Angreifer sogenannte Authentifizierungs-Token, also digitale Zugangsschlüssel von SAP-Mitarbeitern für das Portal erbeutet hätten. Damit könnten sie unter Umständen auf Quellcode zugreifen und ihn verändern.

Nach Handelsblatt-Informationen hat SAP mehrere Gegenmaßnahmen ergriffen. So schränkte der Konzern den Zugriff auf Github ein, stoppte automatisierte Abläufe in der Softwareentwicklung und tauschte Signaturschlüssel aus. Das soll verhindern, dass Angreifer mit bereits erbeuteten Zugangsdaten weiter Zugriff auf Systeme und Quellcode haben.

articleBody:
Built in 1840, this one-room School House served as the educational center for all of the first to eighth grade children in the Hockanum area, later serving only up to sixth grade. This was one of several school houses serving small neighborhood communities around Hadley.

A 1647 Massachusetts law required all towns with 50 or more families to hire a teacher to instruct their children in reading and writing. Parents and students contributed to their school in the form of money, goods, supplies, and chores.

These were one-room schoolhouses, on land that was usually donated. Most schools had one book, the "New England Primer," that was used to teach the alphabet, syllables, and prayer.

The last class to go through this school was in 1933. By then, it was more economical to bus students to the center of town than to keep the neighborhood school houses open.

Along with the outhouse next to it, the Hockanum School House was, and still is, taken care of by the Hockanum community.

articleBody:
> The eval bar on a chess broadcast answers the wrong question. It tells you what happens if two 3600-Elo engines play perfectly with infinite time. What you actually want to know while watching humans play is: who is going to win from here, how likely is a draw, and why?
> HumanFish is an open hybrid model trained on 550,001 tournament positions (91,720 human 2400–2900 games) combining Stockfish 19, Leela Chess Zero, a grandmaster move predictor ( DSC-150M ), and live tournament clocks. It outputs calibrated White Win / Draw / Black Win odds—and shows the concrete moves behind every disagreement right on the board.

I have long wanted such a thing, here is [the link](https://humanfish.vercel.app/methodology). Built by the well-known [book reviewer Patrick Collison](https://chatgpt.com/s/t_6b088852d0288191be4244b86326777b).

articleBody:
# EU-Gipfel: Merz kündigt vorzeitiges Ende der Haushaltsberatungen an

Bild vergrößern Die Präsidentin der Europäischen Kommission, Ursula von der Leyen (r), auf dem EU-Gipfel mit Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU)

Der auf zwei Tage angesetzte EU-Sondergipfel in Brüssel soll überraschend bereits in der Nacht zum Freitag zu Ende gehen. Das kündigte Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz ( CDU ) an. Die Staats- und Regierungschefs würden gegen Mitternacht noch einmal zusammenkommen und den Gipfel anschließend beenden.

»Wir wissen, dass wir heute Abend nicht zu einem Ergebnis kommen«, sagte Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz am Abend in einer Pressekonferenz. Man habe sich darauf verständigt, dass man das Treffen am Freitagvormittag nicht fortsetzen werde.

Bei den Verhandlungen über den künftigen EU-Haushalt gebe es laut Merz neue Bewegung hin zu einer Verringerung des Gesamtvolumens. Schon im Vorfeld hatte sich ein Durchbruch nicht abgezeichnet.

Die sieben sogenannten »sparsamen« Länder bekräftigten nach einem Treffen mit EU-Ratspräsident António Costa auf dem Sondergipfel in Brüssel ihre Position, dass das »Gesamtvolumen« des Budgets für die Jahre von 2028 bis 2034 weiter »angepasst« werden müsse, wie aus deutschen Regierungskreisen verlautete. Der polnische Regierungschef Donald Tusk erklärte unterdessen im Onlinedienst X , ein »billiges Europa« könne sich als »sehr teurer Fehler« erweisen.

### Ukrainehilfe als Voraussetzung

Neben Deutschland gehören Österreich , Dänemark , Schweden , Finnland , Belgien und die Niederlande zur Gruppe der Länder, die sich für eine nur mäßige Erhöhung des künftigen EU-Haushalts im Vergleich zum laufenden Budget einsetzen. Sie fordern zudem das Festhalten an den sogenannten Rabatten, die einige Nettozahlerländer auf ihre Beitragszahlungen erhalten. Eine »nachhaltige und dauerhafte« Finanzierung der Ukraine »durch alle Mitgliedstaaten« sei eine weitere Voraussetzung für diese sieben Länder für einen erfolgreichen Abschluss der Verhandlungen, verlautete aus deutschen Regierungskreisen.

Die Verhandlungen um den Mehrjährigen Finanzrahmen (MFR) für die Jahre 2028 bis 2034 schienen zuletzt festgefahren. Ein Gipfel im Oktober hatte keine Ergebnisse gebracht. Das Sondertreffen am Donnerstag soll nun eine erste Annäherung zwischen den Lagern der »Sparsamen« und der »Freunde der Kohäsion« bringen. Die zweite Gruppe plädiert für einen großen Haushalt, der wie bisher auch den Schwerpunkt auf Agrar- und Regionalförderung legen soll. Ihr gehören unter anderem Italien , Polen und Spanien an.

- Vor den Wahlen in Frankreich und Italien: So ringen Merz, Macron und Meloni um Milliarden für Landwirte 2 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 2 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
- Reise zu CDU-Terminen: Nutzte Merz das Privatflugzeug eines ihm bekannten Sockenherstellers? Von Timo Lehmann und Mayank Sharma 4 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 4 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
- meinung meinung • Umstrittene Militärhilfe für Kyjiw: Der Krieg in der Ukraine kostet die Deutschen viel Geld. Sie fallen zu lassen, wäre noch teurer Der SPIEGEL-Leitartikel von Marina Kormbaki 4 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 4 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
Costa hatte in der vergangenen Woche einen neuen Haushaltsentwurf mit einem Gesamtumfang von rund 1,78 Billionen Euro vorgelegt – rund 204 Milliarden Euro weniger als im Vorschlag der EU-Kommission vom vergangenen Jahr.

articleBody:
Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly [Opportunities Newsletter](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/newsletter/opportunities/).

**[Fall $1,800 Innovate Grants for Art + Photo](https://innovateartistgrants.org)** **Featured**
Innovate Grant awards two $1,800 grants each quarter to one visual artist and one photographer. Nine honorable mentions in each category are also featured on the Innovate Grant platform and join a growing creative community of esteemed artists. Applicants must be 18 years and older, and all media and genres are accepted. All applicants retain the right to the work they submit.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PST on December 15, 2026.**

**[Bryson County Retreat](https://www.brysoncountyretreat.org/)** **Featured**
Practicing artists of any background and at any stage of their career are encouraged to apply for a 2027 residency at Bryson County Retreat. Residency periods can be flexible, but month-long stays are suggested. Bryson County is designed to provide ample living and working space and inspirational settings where an artist may work free from the distractions and responsibilities of day-to-day life. The program includes free lodging near tannic dark water lakes, sprawling live oaks, and drooping Spanish moss at the headwaters of the Santa Fe River in north central Florida.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**Open Calls**

**[Wildlife Photographer of the Year](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/wildlife-photographer-of-the-year/competition.html)** *(International)*
Alongside its conservation message, this prestigious global competition is hosted by London’s Natural History Museum to champion the work of photographers, whether professional or amateur, young or older, or using top-of-the-range equipment or smartphones. Photographers are eligible for myriad awards, with a Grand Title prize of £15,000. The entry fee is £35 (free for Young WPY contest).
**Deadline: 11:30 p.m. GMT on December 3, 2026.**

**[Responsa Foundation Open Call for Textile Art](https://responsafoundation.com/2026/10/13/this-memory-competition/)** *(International)*
The Responsa Foundation champions projects that create meaningful social impact and foster public engagement. The organization is seeking textile artists to submit work for *This Memory,* a group exhibition taking place from September 22 to October 3, 2027, at Burgh House in Hampstead.
**Deadline: December 4, 2026.**

**[Open Call for Public Art Proposals in Moab](https://www.moabarts.org/public-art-application)** (Utah, National)
Moab Arts is accepting proposals for 2027 public art projects. Proposals are welcome for sculpture, murals, three crosswalks, and sticker designs but may include other ideas for different media or locations around the city. Preference is given to local and regional artists.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. MST on December 6, 2026.**

**[Material Works Art Award 2026](https://pci.jotform.com/form/262185636090156)** *(International)*
Material Works supports artists through one-time $2,500 awards in exchange for original pieces added to its growing contemporary art collection. The award recognizes artistic excellence and aims to promote career advancement through increasing visibility and exposure. There is a €40 application fee.
**Deadline: December 6, 2026, or when the first 300 artworks submitted, whichever comes first.**

**[Call for Mail Art](https://www.hivebookarts.org/exhibitions/call-for-mail-art)** *(International)*
Hive Center for the Book Arts in Evanston, Illinois, welcomes mail art for the exhibition *love|mark*, which runs from January 1 to February 27. All submissions must arrive at at the center by December 15 for inclusion in the show.
**Deadline:** **December 15, 2026.**

**[Sony Future Filmmaker Awards](https://www.sonyfuturefilmmakerawards.com/)** *(International)*
The Sony Future Filmmaker Awards is a major program providing opportunities for creators and filmmakers. The shortlisted filmmakers are flown to Sony Pictures Studios in Culver City, California, to attend an awards ceremony and an industry immersion program. Categories include fiction, nonfiction, animation, immersive, student, and vertical format.
**Deadline: 7 a.m. CST on December 15, 2026.**

**[GLEAM 2027 Request for Proposals](https://www.olbrichgleam.org/submit-a-proposal)** *(International)*
Olbrich Botanical Gardens in Madison, Wisconsin, invites proposals for temporary, large-scale, light-based artwork for *GLEAM*, a public art exhibition. The show will be open to the public from August 28 to October 23, 2027.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. CST on January 6, 2027.**

**[Visual Arts Prize IDEA – Vila d’Amer](https://www.ideagc.com/en/idea-mundoarti/)** *(International)*
Apply for this inaugural prize open to artists working in all visual arts media. Two winning artworks, with prizes of €3,500 and €1,500, will become part of the permanent International Visual Arts Collection IDEA – Vila d’Amer.
**Deadline: January 10, 2027.**

**[360 CHICAGO: CloudWalk Call for Artists](https://360chicago.com/cloudwalk-call-for-artists)** *(Chicago)*
One artist will be selected for this major installation in the CloudWalk gallery atop 875 N. Michigan Ave. The selected artist receives a $10,000 commission, and the winning installation will go on view starting April 2027.
**Deadline: January 18, 2027.**

**[World of WearableArt 2027 Competition](https://www.worldofwearableart.com/competition/entry-information)** *(International)*
Entries are now open for the 2027 WOW Competition in Wellington, New Zealand. Awards consist of NZ$200,000 in prizes, including the Supreme WOW Award of NZ$30,000.
**Deadline: February 11, 2027 (international), March 31, 2027 (New Zealand).**

**Grants**

**[The Filmed in Nevada County Grant](https://nevadacityfilmfestival.com/filmedinnc/)** *(International)*
To support filmmakers in the production of work in Nevada County, California, Nevada City Film Festival offers grants between $1,000 and $20,000.
**Deadline: December 1, 2026.**

**[Southern Prize and State Fellowships for Visual Arts](https://www.southarts.org/grants-opportunities/southern-prize-and-state-fellowships-visual-arts)** *(U.S. South)*
The South Arts Southern Prize and State Fellowships acknowledge the highest quality artistic work being created in the American South. The program is open to individual artists living in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee. State Fellowships are $5,000, with one awarded per state. These then compete for two Southern Prize tiers of $25,000 and $10,000.
**Deadline: January 15, 2027 (fee waiver request by December 18, 2026).**

**[The Virigina A. Groot Foundation Grants](https://www.virginiaagrootfoundation.org/grants/)** *(International)*
Each year, the Virginia A. Groot Foundation offers three grants to artists who have exceptional talent and a demonstrated ability in ceramic sculpture or sculpture of diverse mediums. The grants are organized into tiers, with the top award providing $60,000, the second award offering $30,000, and the third awarding $20,000.
**Deadline: January 9, 2027.**

**[Foundation for Contemporary Arts](https://www.foundationforcontemporaryarts.org/grants/emergency-grants/)** **[Emergency Grants](https://www.foundationforcontemporaryarts.org/grants/emergency-grants/)** *(U.S.)*
Emergency Grants provide urgent funding for visual and performing artists and poets who have sudden, unanticipated opportunities to present their work to the public, but there is insufficient time to seek other sources of funding or unexpected expenses are incurred for projects close to completion. Each month, the organization makes approximately 15 to 20 grants in the range of $500 to $3,000 each.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**[National Lottery Project Grants](https://www.artscouncil.org.uk/ProjectGrants/national-lottery-project-grants-guidance-library)** *(U.K.)*
Both individuals and organizations can apply to Arts Council National Lottery Project Grants. These awards are designed to focus on specific projects with starting and ending dates including festivals and carnivals, dance, libraries, literature, museums, music, theater, or visual arts programs. There is no maximum threshold for the fund.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**[Black Artists Grant](https://commonwealthfoundation.com/opportunity/black-artists-grant/)** *(U.K.)*
The Black Artists Grant offered by Creative Debuts is no-strings-attached financial support to help Black artists. Selected applicants receive £500, and applications are reviewed monthly.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**[The Adolf and Esther Gottlieb Emergency Grant](https://www.gottliebfoundation.org/emergency-grant)** *(International)*
This program provides one-time financial assistance to qualified painters, printmakers, and sculptors whose needs resulted from an unforeseen catastrophic incident and who lack the resources to meet that situation. Awardees typically receive $5,000 and up to $15,000.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

[Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grant](https://pkf.org/apply/) * (International)*
The foundation welcomes applications from painters, sculptors, and artists working on paper, including printmakers. Grants are intended for one year and range up to $50,000. The artist’s circumstances determine the size of the grant, and professional exhibition history will be considered.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**Residencies, Fellowships, & More**

**[Kent Cultural Alliance Spring 2027 SERVICE Residency](https://kentculture.org/residency/)** *(U.S.)*
Artists are invited to apply for a six-week residency session in Chestertown, Maryland, devoted to the theme of service. Each selected artist will receive a $7,500 stipend for the six-week session, a travel reimbursement up to $1,000, and studio and gallery expense reimbursement up to $1,500.
**Deadline: 5 p.m. EST on December 1, 2026.**

**[Charles Allis Art Museum Artist in Residence](https://www.charlesallis.org/learn_about/artist_in_residence_/)** *(International)*
Located in Milwaukee’s Lower East Side neighborhood, the Charles Allis Art Museum residency program gives one artist the opportunity to engage with the Allis’ collection of more than 800 historic pieces from the early 20th century. The participant receives an $1,800 honorarium and up to a $400 travel stipend.
**Deadline: December 4, 2026.**

**[2026 McKnight Fellowships for Fiber Artists](https://textilecentermn.org/event/applications-open-for-2026-mcknight-fellowships-for-fiber-artists/)** *(Minnesota)*
Each year, the Textile Center awards two unrestricted $25,000 fellowships to post-emerging Minnesota fiber artists who demonstrate exceptional proficiency, sustained practice, and commitment to the field. Fellowship dates are March 1, 2027, to February 28, 2028.
**Deadline: December 7, 2026.**

**[Open AIR Residencies](https://www.openairmt.org/opportunities)** *(International)*
Open AIR is a Missoula-based nonprofit that brings artists and communities together through place-based residencies and public arts programs across Montana. Sessions currently accepting applications include summer 2027, fall 2027, and spring 2028.
**Deadline: December 7, 2026.**

**[Cove Park Awarded Residencies for 2027-28](https://covepark.org/awarded-residencies-2027-2028/)** *(International)*
Located in beautiful Argyll & Bute, Scotland, Cove Park awards funded residencies, in addition to travel, visa, materials, and access allowances when required. (Self-funded Open Residencies and subsidized winter residencies are open on [a rolling basis](https://covepark.org/current/).)
**Deadline: December 11, 2026.**

**[An Talla Solais Càirdeas/The Kinship Residency](https://www.antallasolais.org/opencall)** *(International)*
BIPOC artists working in any medium are invited to apply to this fully funded residency in Ullapool in the Scottish Highlands. The program runs throughout January, February, and March 2027. The residency covers all work space, housing, mentoring, and exhibition costs in addition to a £750 weekly stipend.
**Deadline: December 14, 2026.**

**[Joshua Tree Highlands Artist Residency 2027-28](https://www.jthar.org/)** *(International)*
Joshua Tree Highlands Artist Residency offers time and space amidst the natural beauty of Joshua Tree National Park. Seven-week residencies include scholarship funds, housing, and studio space designed to accommodate a broad range of artistic activity and open studio events. There is a $45 application fee.
**Deadline: December 15, 2026.**

**[ren AiR](https://www.ren.global/air)** *(International)*
ren is a discovery platform where you share everything that goes into your artistic practice. For its residency, four selected artists will each receive $5,000 to develop and realize a project of their choice, wherever they are based, while sharing their creative journey with the ren community. In addition, eight artists will receive $2,000 prizes.
**Deadline: December 31, 2026.**

**[Ox-Bow Summer Fellowship](https://www.ox-bow.org/fellowship-program)** *(International)*
The Ox-Bow Summer Fellowship offers twelve weeks to slow down and deepen your practice within a creative community. The program will welcome 18 fellows and is open to senior BFA students, MFA students, postgraduates, and artists with comparable professional experience.
**Deadline: January 7, 2027.**

**[Fine Arts Work Center Seven-Month Residency](https://fawc.org/apply/)** *(International)*
The Fine Arts Work Center in Provincetown grants 10 annual fellowships each to visual artists and writers for a seven-month residency that runs from October 1 to April 30. Visual arts fellows are provided with a private furnished apartment and a separate studio, a $1,300 monthly stipend, plus a $1,000 exit stipend to support relocation at the end of the fellowship. There is a $55 application fee until midday on December 1, then $65 until the opportunity closes.
**Deadline: February 6, 2027.**

**[Smithereen Farm Winter Residency](https://www.smithereenfarm.com/winter-residency/)** *(International)*
Smithereen Farm offers affordable, shared, winter housing to farmers and agrarian-adjacent people and creatives. In the winter, its studio spaces and rooms in shared houses are generally rented for $350 per month, which includes access to common rooms, space for studio work or desks, utilities, fast Wi-Fi at Reversing Hall, a carpenter shop, sewing machines, video projection space, and access to the farm’s agricultural library.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**[Jackrabbit Studios Residency](https://tally.so/r/RGq2yJ)** *(International)*
Jackrabbit Studios is a creative sanctuary and retreat space in the Southern California High Desert that welcomes creatives, healing arts practitioners, and facilitators at any stage of practice to our five acres of secluded and sublime desert expanse to craft a residency tailored to your season of practice. Fees range from $450 per week to $2,000 per week, and pets are welcome for an additional fee.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

articleBody:
The sight of a spiky sea urchin wandering along the floor of the ocean wearing a hat is quite comical, and even more so when it's a bunch of them (I don't know the collective noun for sea urchins) sped up in a time-lapse. They are all wearing a variety of hats that are really rocks, shells, and other ocean debris. Some wear several of these hats at once. One even carries a shell with a hermit crab living in it! But why do they do that? And how did they learn this new behavior? Even then, how did the trend spread among the herd when they don't have eyes or brains the way we think of those organs?

In this clip from the new BBC nature series *Blue Planet III*, Sir David Attenborough narrates a sea urchin fashion show and explains what benefit this adaptation gives these brainless sea creatures. -via [Born in Space](https://www.borninspace.com/)

articleBody:
HANAU. **Wegen familiärer Probleme wollte er der Jugendlichen angeblich «Therapiestunden» geben. Schließlich werden er und sein Opfer laut Anklage vom Hausmeister überrascht: Ein Lehrer aus Hessen muss sich nun wegen Missbrauchs vor Gericht verantworten. Kein Einzelfall: Erst in der vergangenen Woche war ein Gymnasiallehrer aus Thüringen wegen** **sexuellen Missbrauchs einer Schülerin zu einer hohen Gefängnisstrafe verurteilt worden.**

Das Gericht hat zu entscheiden. (Symbolfoto.) Foto: Shutterstock / travelview

Vor dem Landgericht Hanau hat der Prozess gegen einen Lehrer begonnen, der eine Schülerin mehrfach sexuell missbraucht haben soll. In einem Fall wirft die Staatsanwaltschaft ihm sogar vor, die zum Tatzeitpunkt 15-Jährige vergewaltigt haben.

Der verbeamtete Lehrer soll im vergangenen Jahr das Vertrauen der Schülerin zunächst unter dem Vorwand erschlichen haben, ihr wegen familiärer Probleme «Therapiestunden» zu geben. Nach Annäherungen soll es nach Angaben der Staatsanwaltschaft zu Küssen und sexuellen Handlungen gekommen sein. Tatorte seien die Schule, ein Wald und eine Wiese gewesen. Ans Licht kam der Missbrauch laut Anklage, als ein Hausmeister im August vergangenen Jahres den Lehrer und die Schülerin in einer Toilette überraschte.

Über seinen Anwalt räumte der nach eigenen Angaben vom Schuldienst suspendierte 48-Jährige sämtliche Missbrauchsfälle ein, bestritt jedoch die Vergewaltigung. Zum Schutz der Minderjährigen schloss das Gericht vor deren Zeugenvernehmung die Öffentlichkeit aus. Der Prozess soll bis Mitte Dezember fortgesetzt werden.

Zahlreiche Missbrauchsfälle in Schulen haben in den vergangenen Monaten für Schlagzeilen gesorgt – zuletzt die Verurteilung eines Gymnasiallehrers aus Thüringen zu sechs Jahren Haft ([News4teachers berichtete](https://www.news4teachers.de/2026/11/schon-wieder-missbrauch-schon-wieder-muss-ein-gymnasiallehrer-ins-gefaengnis/)). *News4teachers / mit Material der dpa*

articleBody:
# Bachs Weihnachtsoratorium in der Martin-Luther-Kirche - Neustadt-Geflüster

Mit Pauken, Trompeten und „Jauchzet, frohlocket“ beginnt am Sonnabend, 12. Dezember, um 19.30 Uhr das Weihnachtsoratorium von Johann Sebastian Bach in der Martin-Luther-Kirche. Unter der Leitung von Elke Voigt erklingen die ersten drei Kantaten des Werkes. Dresdner Bachchor unter der leitung von Elke Voigt – Foto: Kirchgemeinde Traditionell erklingen die ersten drei Kantaten in der Martin-Luther-Kirche am Sonnabend vor dem dritten Advent. Der Dresdner Bachchor, ein eigens zusammengestellter Jugendchor und die Sinfonietta Dresden gestalten den Konzertabend. Als Solistinnen und Solisten wirken Heidi Maria Taubert (Sopran), Ewa Zeuner (Alt), Jonas Finger (Tenor) und Cornelius Uhle (Bass) mit. An ausgewählten Stellen kann das Publikum in die Choräle einstimmen. Fast 300 Jahre Weihnachtsmusik Johann Sebastian Bach komponierte sein Weihnachtsoratorium 1734 als Leipziger Thomaskantor. Anders als heute üblich, erklangen die sechs Kantaten damals nicht an einem Abend, sondern an sechs verschiedenen Festtagen zwischen Weihnachten und dem Dreikönigstag. articleBody:
Alice’s Restaurant. It’s now a Thanksgiving classic, and something of a tradition around here. Recorded in 1967, the 18+ minute counterculture song recounts Arlo Guthrie’s real encounter with the law, starting on Thanksgiving Day 1965. As the long song unfolds, we hear all about how a hippie-bating police officer, by the name of [William “Obie” Obanhein](http://www.nytimes.com/1994/09/14/obituaries/william-j-obanhein-alice-s-restaurant-lawman-69.html), arrested Arlo for littering. (Cultural footnote: Obie previously posed for several Norman Rockwell paintings, including the well-known painting, [“The Runaway,”](http://www.artchive.com/artchive/r/rockwell/rockwell_runaway.jpg) that graced a [1958 cover of](https://web.archive.org/web/20180723115710/https://www.saturdayeveningpost.com/2012/05/08/archives/a-fond-farewell-to-an-iconic-policeman.html) *[The Saturday Evening Post](https://web.archive.org/web/20180723115710/https://www.saturdayeveningpost.com/2012/05/08/archives/a-fond-farewell-to-an-iconic-policeman.html)*.) In fairly short order, Arlo pleads guilty to a misdemeanor charge, pays a $25 fine, and cleans up the thrash. But the story isn’t over. Not by a long shot.

Later, when Arlo (son of Woody Guthrie) gets called up for the draft, the petty crime ironically becomes a basis for disqualifying him from military service in the Vietnam War. Guthrie recounts this with some bitterness as the song builds into a satirical protest against the war: “I’m sittin’ here on the Group W bench ’cause you want to know if I’m moral enough to join the Army, burn women, kids, houses and villages after bein’ a litterbug.” And then we’re back to the cheery chorus again: “You can get anything you want, at Alice’s Restaurant.”

We have featured Guthrie’s classic during past years. But, for this Thanksgiving, we give you the illustrated version.

It’s hard to rely 100% on ads, and your [contributions](https://bit.ly/3EBHjtX) will help us continue providing the best free cultural and educational materials to learners everywhere. title: Six Factors That Support Mental Health for Black Youth
subtitle: On a summer day at UC Berkeley, four teenagers jostled at a whiteboard, vying to write down their solutions to an important public health concern.

articleBody:
On a summer day at UC Berkeley, four teenagers jostled at a whiteboard, vying to write down their solutions to an important public health concern. They were having fun even as they took on a heavy task: helping researchers design programs to reduce the skyrocketing suicide rate among Black youth.

In the United States, deaths by suicide have been surging among Black kids and teens for decades. For those between 10 and 17 years of age, the suicide rate [rose 144% from 2007 to 2020](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/sites/default/files/2023-08/2023-august-still-ringing-alarm.pdf). What’s more, Black boys die by suicide more than twice as frequently as Black girls, although the suicide rate for Black girls [increased by 182% between 2001 and 2017](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10900-019-00678-x).

As the teenagers brainstormed, [Jasmin Brooks Stephens](https://psychology.berkeley.edu/people/jasmin-brooks-stephens), a Berkeley assistant professor of psychology, watched nearby. The moment was a highlight in research she was conducting with the Homeless Children’s Network on improving mental health outcomes for Black youth. Brooks Stephens believed that teens themselves have meaningful ideas to share, and she had worked for eight weeks with these particular teenagers, who were part of the network’s [Jabali Youth Advocacy](https://www.hcnkids.org/jabali-youth-advocacy) organization, culminating in their trip to campus.

“One of the most exciting things was seeing them all jump up and say, ‘Wait, we can make a program for making us feel better? We have the power to do that?’” Brooks Stephens recalled. “Seeing them find and discover that sense of agency in themselves—that was invaluable to me.” It also was one of the few times any of the teens had visited a college campus, she said, an added bonus. In future work, Brooks Stephens plans to translate the results of her study for clinicians and policymakers who are trying to improve suicide prevention for Black youth.

The ongoing project is just one example of how Brooks Stephens is working to address rising suicide rates among Black youth by engaging them in participatory research—an unusual and hopeful approach in suicide prevention studies. “This summer I had the incredible opportunity to work alongside young people to design a program that would help other young people want to live,” she said. “Rather than waiting until a young person is already in crisis, I’m interested in understanding what helps youth thrive—what gives them hope and a sense of possibility and helps them recognize the brilliance they have inside them.”

## A pathway to hope in the face of racism

Despite the growing crisis among Black youth, [suicide rates are dropping for adolescents in the U.S. overall](https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/reports/rpt57150/2025-nsduh-annual-national-report.pdf). Brooks Stephens finds these statistics revealing: “To me, that suggests that the approaches we have relied on have not adequately addressed the conditions driving suicide risk in Black communities,” she said.

It’s easy to talk about [structural racism](https://news.berkeley.edu/2025/08/14/watch-berkeley-scholar-explain-structural-racism/) as an abstract concept, or personal encounters with racists as disturbing but bounded moments. But grappling with racism heavily impacts Black youth and increases their suicide risk, according to a 2023 report from the [Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/sites/default/files/2023-08/2023-august-still-ringing-alarm.pdf). Indeed, Brooks Stephens has published work documenting how racial discrimination and the COVID-19 pandemic, which disproportionately harmed Black Americans, together [worsened suicide risk for Black young adults](https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2025-01327-001).

Brooks Stephens’s work is informed by both her research and her own experience of how race can shape young people’s sense of self. “I became aware very early on that Black children are often navigating expectations about who they are supposed to be before they have even had the opportunity to figure out who they are for themselves,” she said. “That has stayed with me—the importance of creating space for Black young people to define themselves, recognize their strengths, and imagine who they want to become.” At the same time, she saw how the stigma surrounding mental health could make it harder for Black youth and families to seek support, even as racism and other chronic stressors were impacting their well-being.

When she took an African American psychology class as an undergraduate at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, with Enrique Neblett, a renowned scholar of race and health who became her mentor, Brooks Stephens saw the connection between those experiences—and found her passion. “I realized that there was an entire field devoted to understanding how racism affects mental health and how Black children come to understand themselves and their racial identity,” she said.

Later, during her doctoral research at the University of Houston, Brooks Stephens worked with Rheeda Walker, an expert on suicide science and African American adult mental health research. Brooks Stephens noticed that there was very limited discussion about building upstream resilience in suicide prevention research—an approach that focuses on child well-being and happiness before the development of a mental health crisis.

“We’re studying why people choose to end their life without understanding what makes people want to live,” she said. For Brooks Stephens, that realization opened up a different way of thinking about suicide prevention, one that made room for the strengths that were often absent from traditional models, such as racial identity, spirituality, family connection, belonging, or hope.

## Focusing on strengths to prevent suicide

Brooks Stephens knows she can’t single-handedly eliminate the racial traumas faced by young Black people. Nor can she end other factors that lead to higher suicide rates in her community, such as systemic injustice or poverty. Instead, she’s focusing on where she can make a difference through her research.

“While I may not be able to eradicate racism, I can help build programs that change how Black young people see themselves and their futures—programs that help them feel grounded in their identity and able to imagine a life that feels worth living,” she said.

*Brooks Stephens and her colleagues identified six positive factors that reduce suicidality among Black youth (courtesy of Jasmin Brooks Stephens).*

As a first step, this year she and her colleagues created the [Black Youth Thriving Framework for Suicide Prevention](https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2027-42684-001). It’s based on a literature review that identified six protective factors that can reduce suicidality among Black youth, including family support, community ties, and self-acceptance. “What we’re working to identify now are the strategies that can help cultivate those strengths in young people’s lives,” Brooks Stephens said.

Already, in a [study from 2023](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/00957984211037440), she and her colleagues showed that Black young adults with stronger feelings of self-acceptance are less vulnerable to depression and suicide. Likewise, she has identified [mindfulness and meditation as potential tools](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12671-023-02180-x) for Black Americans in their early 20s to buffer the impulsivity that is often associated with suicide risk.

This approach is a radical departure from the status quo. Right now, resources for preventing suicide orbit around moments of crisis, Brooks Stephens said. When a child shows signs of depression or arrives at a hospital following a suicide attempt, that’s when an intervention is often provided. Brooks Stephens wants to develop research-backed ways to prevent a child from ever getting to that troubling point in the first place.

And, increasingly, she is asking Black young people themselves to help determine what those approaches should look like. Brooks Stephens said that the four teens with whom she worked this summer were not simply research participants; they were collaborators in imagining what suicide prevention could become.

“It’s very uplifting for me because I’m bringing underserved voices into our research and I’m designing solutions,” she said. “And those solutions are how we make kids want to live and love themselves. That’s it. It’s loving themselves, loving their life. That’s what I’m helping them discover.”

This article was originally published on [Berkeley News](https://news.berkeley.edu). Read the [original article](https://news.berkeley.edu/2026/10/07/as-the-suicide-rate-grows-among-black-youth-heres-where-a-berkeley-researcher-sees-reason-for-hope/).

articleBody:
### “The self is a style of being, continually expanding in a vital process of definition, affirmation, revision, and growth…”

*“No one can build you the bridge on which you, and only you, must cross the river of life,”* thirty-year-old Nietzsche wrote in his treatise on [how to find yourself](https://www.themarginalian.org/2015/09/30/nietzsche-find-yourself-schopenhauer-as-educator/). And yet in the century and a half since, a curious dissonance has begun to reverberate across culture: On the one hand, we have grown increasingly fixated on the self as the focal lens for interpreting the world — a fixation which Ian McEwan [so brilliantly satirized](https://www.themarginalian.org/2016/10/03/ian-mcewan-nutshell-selfhood/) and which has precipitated today’s tragic epidemic of militant identity politics; on the other hand, the rise of neuroscience has demonstrated again and again that the self we experience as so overwhelmingly real — the psychophysiological raft of experience through which we float along the river of life — [is a sensory-perceptual byproduct of consciousness](https://www.themarginalian.org/2017/05/25/christof-koch-consciousness-qualia/), completely illusory in its solidity.

Nearly half a century ago, the Pulitzer-winning poet **Robert Penn Warren** (April 24, 1905–September 15, 1989) cast a cautionary eye to the notion of “finding oneself” in [Democracy and Poetry](https://www.amazon.com/Democracy-Poetry-Jefferson-lecture-humanities/dp/0674196252/?tag=braipick-20) ([public library](http://www.worldcat.org/title/democracy-and-poetry/oclc/471794841&referer=brief_results)) — his magnificent Jefferson Lecture about [power, tenderness, and art’s role in a healthy society](https://www.themarginalian.org/2017/05/22/robert-penn-warren-democracy-and-poetry/).

Robert Penn Warren

Decades before Harvard psychologist Daniel Gilbert’s witty and wise observation that [“human beings are works in progress that mistakenly think they’re finished,”](https://www.themarginalian.org/2014/06/18/daniel-gilbert-happiness-future-self/) Warren challenges the cultural trend of young people taking “time off” from school or work in order to “get away from it all” and find themselves. He writes:

> In the phrase [“to find myself”] lurks the idea that the self is a pre-existing entity, a self like a Platonic idea existing in a mystic realm beyond time and change. No, rather an object like a nugget of gold in the placer pan, the Easter egg under the bush at an Easter-egg hunt, a four-leaf clover to promise miraculous luck. Here is the essence of passivity, one’s quintessential luck. And the essence of absurdity, too, for the self is never to be found, but must be created, not the happy accident of passivity, but the product of a thousand actions, large and small, conscious or unconscious, performed not “away from it all,” but in the face of “it all,” for better or for worse, in work and leisure rather than in free time.

In consonance with my own deep belief in [the ongoingness and fluidity of our becoming](https://onbeing.org/programs/maria-popova-cartographer-of-meaning-in-a-digital-age/), Warren adds:

> The self is a style of being, continually expanding in a vital process of definition, affirmation, revision, and growth, a process that is the image, we may say, of the life process of a healthy society itself.

In a sentiment that calls to mind Academy of American Poets executive director Jennifer Benka’s beautiful observation that [“poems are physical sites of discovery and sense-records of our humanity,”](https://www.themarginalian.org/2017/05/29/the-universe-in-verse/) Warren considers the role of poetry as a locus of our evolving being:

> How does poetry come into all this? By being an antidote, a sovereign antidote, for passivity. For the basic fact about poetry is that it demands participation, from the secret physical echo in muscle and nerve that identifies us with the medium, to the imaginative enactment that stirs the deepest recesses where life-will and values reside. Beyond that, it nourishes our life-will in the process of testing our values. And this is not to be taken as implying a utilitarian aesthetic. It is, rather, one way of describing our pleasure in poetry as an adventure in the celebration of life.

Complement this particular portion of Warren’s thoroughly transcendent [Democracy and Poetry](https://www.amazon.com/Democracy-Poetry-Jefferson-lecture-humanities/dp/0674196252/?tag=braipick-20) with Walt Whitman on [identity and the paradox of the self](https://www.themarginalian.org/2016/06/24/walt-whitman-democratic-vistas-self/) and philosopher Rebecca Goldstein on [what makes you and your childhood self the “same” person despite a lifetime of change](https://www.themarginalian.org/2014/10/07/rebecca-goldstein-personal-identity/), then revisit Elizabeth Alexander on [what poetry does for the human spirit](https://www.themarginalian.org/2015/07/29/elizabeth-alexander-ars-poetica-100-i-believe/).

### donating = loving

For seventeen years, I have been spending hundreds of hours and thousands of dollars each month composing *The Marginalian* (which [bore the outgrown name Brain Pickings](https://www.themarginalian.org/2021/10/22/brain-pickings-becoming-the-marginalian/) for its first fifteen years). It has remained free and ad-free and alive thanks to patronage from readers. I have no staff, no interns, no assistant — a thoroughly one-woman labor of love that is also my life and my livelihood. If this labor makes your own life more livable in any way, please consider lending a helping hand with a [donation](https://www.themarginalian.org/donate/). Your support makes all the difference.

### newsletter

*The Marginalian* has a free weekly newsletter. It comes out on Sundays and offers the week’s most inspiring reading. Here’s [what to expect](https://mailchi.mp/brainpickings/janna-levin-rebecca-elson-anne-lamott-james-gleick). Like? [Sign up.](https://www.themarginalian.org/newsletter/)

articleBody: Background: The developments in generative AI (GenAI) are expected to have a substantial impact on the field of mental health, including the delivery of clinical services and the role of psychologists. However, there is limited knowledge about how psychologists use and perceive GenAI, including its potential, risks, and effects on the future role of psychologists and professional practice. This includes the competency levels among psychologists and factors associated with the intention to use GenAI within the psychology profession. Objective: This study examined the use of GenAI, self-rated digital and GenAI competencies, behavioral intention to use GenAI, and perceptions of its future impact on professional practice among psychology students, internship psychologists, and licensed psychologists in Sweden. Methods: A national cross-sectional online survey was conducted from January to February 2026 in collaboration with the Swedish Psychological Association. The 36-item survey included closed and open-ended questions, including Likert scale, nominal scale, and multiple-choice items. A total of 1077 respondents, with 64.7% (n=697) being women and with a mean age of 45.5 years (SD 13.7), were included in the analyses. Responses were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods, including hierarchical multiple linear regression, ANOVA, and correlational analysis. articleBody:
**Kurz vor dem Ende der Cyber Deals legt Thomann noch einmal nach und reduziert bis zum 30.11.2026 zahlreiche Synthesizer, Sequencer und Grooveboxen.**

Thomann Synthesizer Cyber Deals (Bildquelle: Bonedo Grafik)

## Thomann Cyber Deals

Kurz vor dem Ende der Cyber Days legt Thomann noch einmal nach und reduziert zahlreiche Synthesizer, Sequencer und Grooveboxen. Bis zum 30.11.2026 könnt ihr weiterhin kräftig sparen. Es lohnt sich also, die Angebote genauer unter die Lupe zu nehmen. Im Bereich Synthesizer sind jetzt sogar noch einige neue Deals hinzugekommen, die wir euch hier vorstellen. Schaut auch regelmäßig auf der Thomann-Website vorbei, damit euch kein Angebot entgeht!

Endlich ist es wieder so weit! Wie jedes Jahr präsentiert Thomann die Cyber Deals, die ab heute bis einschließlich **30. November 2026, 23:59 Uhr,** erhältlich sind!

Jetzt lohnt es sich zuzuschlagen! Wie wäre es mit dem lang ersehnten Instrument oder einem musikalischen Geschenk zu Weihnachten: Mit Rabatten von bis zu 70 Prozent bieten die [Thomann Cyber Deals](https://www.thomann.de/intl/special_cyber-deals.html) die perfekte Gelegenheit, um musikalische Wünsche wahr werden zu lassen.

## Cyber Deals: Synthesizer, Grooveboxen und mehr Cyber Deals

Selbstverständlich hat Thomann auch an die Synthesizer gedacht, und wir haben es uns nicht nehmen lassen, euch einige ausgewählte Deals vorzustellen. Ob Sound-Designer, Klangschrauber, Beat-Produzenten, Bedroom-Producer: Ihr werdet sicher einen guten Deal finden!

Wir empfehlen euch aber dringend, auch die [Thomann Cyber Deals](https://www.thomann.de/intl/special_cyber-deals.html)-Website zu besuchen und die Angebote in Ruhe zu durchstöbern.

Mit dabei sind zahlreiche Top-Marken aus unterschiedlichsten Kategorien, darunter Akai, Behringer, Beyerdynamic, Epiphone, Focusrite, Gibson, Harley Benton, JBL, Martin Guitar, Millenium, PRS, Sennheiser, Shure und Yamaha.

**Wer die Thomann Cyber Deals nicht verpassen möchte, sollte schnell sein: Die besten Angebote können rasch vergriffen sein: Hier geht es zu den [Deals.](https://www.thomann.de/intl/special_cyber-deals.html)**

Inhalte

- Thomann Cyber Deals
- Cyber Deals: Synthesizer, Grooveboxen und mehr Cyber Deals
- Teenage Engineering OP-XY
- Mehr Teenage Engineering Deals
- Pittsburgh Modular Taiga Keyboard
- Pittsburgh Modular Voltage Lab 2
- Roland TR-1000 und Thon Case Roland TR-1000
- Arturia AstroLab 61 Silver

- Weitere Deals

## Teenage Engineering OP-XY

Auch von Teenage Engineering gibt es noch einmal einige interessante Angebote. **Die Groovebox OP-XY ist von 2.055,00 Euro auf 1.699,00 Euro reduziert.**

[Hier geht es zum Teenage Engineering OP-XY Test.](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/teenage-engineering-op-xy-test/)

## Mehr Teenage Engineering Deals

Wer generell Interesse an Produkten von Teenage Engineering hat und nicht nur auf Synthesizer steht, sollte bei Thomann unbedingt folgende Deals beachten. **Der portable Profimixer TX-6**kostet jetzt**899,00 Euro**statt regulär 1.019,00 Euro. Auch der**TP-7 Multitrack Field Recorder**ist deutlich günstiger erhältlich. Er kann bis zu drei Stereospuren gleichzeitig aufnehmen und wiedergeben und kostet während der Cyber Days**1.199,00 Euro** statt 1.444,00 Euro.

Passend zum portablen Recorder und Mixer gibt es auch das tragbare **Großmembran Kondensatormikrofon CM-15**zum Sonderpreis. Statt 1.199,00 Euro werden dafür aktuell nur**899,00 Euro**fällig. Abgerundet werden die Angebote durch den**Hi-End-Bluetooth-Lautsprecher OB-4.**Dieser kostet normalerweise 531,00 Euro und ist jetzt für**409,00 Euro** erhältlich.

## Pittsburgh Modular Taiga Keyboard

Ein echtes Highlight unter den aktuellen Angeboten ist das Taiga Keyboard von Pittsburgh Modular. Der semimodulare Analog-Synthesizer verfügt über drei Oszillatoren, ein Multimode-Filter und zahlreiche Möglichkeiten zur Klangbearbeitung. Über das Patchfeld lassen sich die einzelnen Komponenten flexibel miteinander verbinden und modulieren.

[Hier geht es zum Pittsburgh Modular Taiga Keyboard und Desktop Test](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/pittsburgh-taiga-keyboard-test/)

**Das Taiga Keyboard kostet normalerweise 1.169,00 Euro und ist jetzt für nur 799,00 Euro erhältlich.**

## Pittsburgh Modular Voltage Lab 2

Ebenfalls reduziert ist das Pittsburgh Modular Voltage Lab 2. Das semimodulare Analogsynthesizersystem kombiniert verschiedene Oszillatoren, Modulationsquellen und Effekte mit einem integrierten Touch-Controller und Sequencer. Es richtet sich vor allem an experimentierfreudige Sounddesigner und Modular-Fans.

**Statt regulär 1.852,00 Euro kostet es derzeit nur 1.499,00 Euro.**

## Torso Electronics T-1

Ihr wolltet schon immer einen Sequencer mit 16 Spuren und 16 MIDI-Kanälen? Dann solltet ihr euch den Torso Electronics T-1 genauer anschauen. Jede Spur lässt sich wahlweise als euklidischer Drum-Sequencer, monophoner oder polyphoner Noten-Sequencer oder Arpeggiator konfigurieren. Damit ist der T-1 ein vielseitiges Werkzeug für die Steuerung von Hardware-Synthesizern und Drumcomputern.

[Hier geht es zum Torso Electronics T-1 Test.](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/torso-electronics-t-1-test/)

**Bei Thomann ist der Torso Electronics T-1 bis zum 30.11.2026 von 550,00 Euro auf 449,00 Euro reduziert. Das Angebot gilt für die weiße und schwarze Ausgabe.**

## Roland TR-1000 und Thon Case Roland TR-1000

Mit der TR-1000 hat Roland eine echte State of the Art Drum-Machine auf den Markt gebracht, die all die interessanten Features vereint, welche die legendären Roland Drum Machines TR-808, TR-909 und weitere Klassiker berühmt gemacht haben. Die TR-1000 verfügt über eine analoge und eine digitale Klangerzeugung. Außerdem kann sie mithilfe der VA-Synthese Bass- und Synthesizer-Sounds erzeugen und auch sampeln.

**Der Preis der Roland TR-1000 bleibt während der Cyber Deals unverändert bei 2.699,00 Euro. Thomann legt euch allerdings das passende Thon Case Roland TR-1000 kostenlos dazu, für das normalerweise weitere 225,00 Euro fällig werden. Dabei handelt es sich um ein maßgeschneidertes Case für die TR-1000, das auch für den Tournee-Einsatz ausgelegt ist.**

Hier geht es zum [Roland TR-1000 Test](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/roland-tr-1000-test/)

## Arturia AstroLab 61 Silver

Normalerweise müsst ihr 2.435,00 Euro für die Akai MPC XL zahlen. Doch jetzt habt ihr die Gelegenheit, diese Powerworkstation für nur **2.199,00 Euro**zu erwerben. Das entspricht einer**Ersparnis von 236,00 Euro.**
